title: Quality you can trust, safe relaxers and numbers that pay

say: Quality you can trust, safe relaxers, and numbers that pay.
This is the video for module three of Hair Care and Simple Styling.
Clients judge your work twice: in the mirror on the day, and when they take the style down weeks later. Healthy edges win that second moment, and that is what brings them back.

panel.heading: The six-point finish check
items: Parts straight and even
Braids the same size
Comfortable, no pain
Edges not pulled
Ends neat and sealed
Scalp clean, no residue

say: So before she leaves, check six things. Parts straight. Braids the same size. No pain. Edges not pulled. Ends neat and sealed. Scalp clean.
Stand back an arm's length first, then look closely at the hairline, nape and behind the ears. Ask her to move her head, because tight braids often only hurt when she moves.

say: Traction alopecia is hair loss from repeated pulling. It shows first at the temples and front hairline. Early on it can recover, but if pulling continues, follicles can scar and the hair may not grow back.
These are the habits that cause it.

panel.heading: Mistakes that damage hair
left: Very tight edges for a sleek look
Styles left in three months or more
right: Lighter tension, leave baby hairs out
Take down within four to eight weeks

say: Use lighter tension at the front. Match extension hair to the size of the section. Advise takedown within about four to eight weeks.
And never send a client home with braids that hurt. Pain is the root being pulled. Loosen or redo it.

say: Lye and no-lye relaxers are both strong alkalis that can burn. Train with an experienced stylist first, and follow the exact product's instructions.
Step one. Consult and check the scalp.

panel.heading: Relaxer safety, step by step
items: Consult and check the scalp
Strand test as the product says
Gloves on; base cream on hairline and ears
Apply only to new growth
Time it exactly; if it burns, rinse now
Rinse, neutralise fully, condition, record

say: If there are cuts, sores, scratches or irritation, do not relax. Ask clients not to scratch or brush hard for a day or two before.

say: If relaxer gets into the eyes, rinse immediately with clean running water for at least 15 minutes, and get medical help.

cards.d: Rinse at once with clean running water for at least 15 minutes. Get medical help.
Rinse at once with lots of water and advise a clinic visit.
Explain risks, write the consent on her card. No relaxers on children.

say: If the scalp burns or blisters, rinse at once with lots of water and advise a clinic visit. Keep relaxers locked away from children.

say: Many talented braiders are always busy but never have money. Write one line in a log after every client: style, hours, price, materials, payment and source.
Profit per service is the price minus materials.

panel.heading: Four numbers to watch
items: Profit per service: price minus materials
Earnings per hour: profit divided by hours
Repeat rate: repeat clients over all clients
Client sources: how new clients found you

say: Earnings per hour is profit divided by hours. This shows which styles truly pay.

card.title: Which style pays best?

say: Medium knotless braids, with the client bringing the hair, cost 20,000 naira. Materials are 800, so profit is 19,200.

say: It takes 5 hours, so that is 3,840 naira per hour. Cornrows give her about 3,130 per hour, and wash and twists only 2,440.
So Bisi raises her wash-and-twist price a little and promotes knotless braids on WhatsApp.

say: To remember. Run the six-point check every time. Pain, bumps and tenting are warnings, not normal. Relax only a healthy scalp, and only new growth. Record consent. And log every client, so you know what truly pays.
